answer: Reputation minted through costly, slow stake earns weight, so one identity faked a thousand times still costs real capital each time. Like velvet worn smooth only by years of friction, trust accrues per verified act, not per account. New sybils arrive as cheap as shale, yet each must burn time-stamped stake before voting. The ocean of clones thus thins into few weighted voices, and the attacker's bottleneck becomes capital at scale.
